newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations in Italy under 50 pct -JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations in Italy under 50 pct -JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad- based start to European monetary union in 1999 edged lower this week, with the perceived probability of Italy taking part dipping below 50 percent, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed.
Market prices indicating the probability of Italy joining Germany and France in the first wave of EMU fell six points to 49 percent, according to the U.S. investment firm's "EMU calculator."
Jitters last week about the probability of Belgium starting monetary union calmed however, with the assigned probability there nudging back up to 99 percent from 97 last week.
The calculator showed the probability of France starting EMU remains 100 percent.
JP Morgan point out there is a reasonable margin of error in probability levels of between three and five points.
Elsewhere, expectations of EMU participation by other non-core countries, which have retreated steadily over the past two months, edged slightly lower.
The probabilities assigned to Portugal, Finland, Denmark, Sweden and the UK all slipped, although by less than five points. Probabilities in Spain and Ireland were unchanged.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
